newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CUBS EDGE GIANTS IN BRAWL-MARRED GAME.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CUBS EDGE GIANTS IN BRAWL-MARRED GAME.

text.p: Sammy Sosa's two-run double in the seventh inning put the Chicago Cubs ahead for good in a brawl-marred 6-5 victory over the San Francisco Giants Wednesday.
Sosa's 26th homer of the season had knotted the game 1-1 in the fourth.

With the Cubs leading 2-1 in the fourth, starter Jeremi Gonzalez hit leadoff batter Jeff Kent with a fastball. Kent tore the mask off catcher Tyler Houston's face after a heated exchange. The two grappled as both benches emptied. Kent and Houston were ejected.

"He physically took my mask off," said Houston. "As far as I know, he's going to hit me. He was pretty upset and there's always a lot of adrenaline on a baseball field when someone gets hit. You can say what you want to someone, but when you get physical, that's a problem."
Gonzalez (9-5) allowed four runs and seven hits over 6 1/3 innings to beat the Giants for the second time in seven days.
"I'm not trying to hit anybody," Gonzalez said. "I'm just trying to pitch my game."

Terry Adams allowed a pair of two-out baserunners in the ninth but a little luck got him his 10th save in 12 chances when Jose Vizcaino hit a line drive up the middle that Adams deflected to shortstop Jose Hernandez, who forced Hamilton at second to end the game.
Dave Clark and Kevin Orie also homered for the Cubs.
San Francisco starter Mark Gardner (12-6) took the loss.
Stan Javier and Bill Mueller homered for the Giants, whose lead over the Dodgers in the National League West shrank to 1 1/2 games.

In Los Angeles, rookie Adam Riggs, hitless in his first eight major-league at-bats, snapped a 1-1 tie with his first career RBI and Tom Candiotti gave up three hits over seven innings as the Dodgers beat the Montreal Expos 3-1.

Candiotti (9-4) gave up one run, walked one and struck out a season-high seven to win for the fourth time in his last five starts. His only mistake was Mike Lansing's sixth-inning homer. Todd Zeile homered for the Dodgers,.
In Atlanta, Jon Lieber allowed one run over 6 1/3 innings and combined with two relievers to outduel John Smoltz as the Pittsburgh Pirates edged the Braves 2-1.

Dale Sveum and Turner Ward drove in runs for Pittsburgh, which has held Atlanta to three runs in the first two games of the series. Rich Loiselle survived his own fielding error to record his 20th save in 22 opportunities.
Lieber (7-12) snapped a personal four-game losing streak.
Smoltz (11-10) threw a seven-hitter but had his four-game winning streak halted.
The Braves split their eight-game homestand and had their lead over Florida in the N.L. East reduced to five games.

In Houston, Jeff Conine's two-run single in the top of the eighth sparked a four-run rally and lifted the Florida Marlins to an 8-6 victory over the Astros, who had a four-game winning streak snapped.
The Marlins began the eighth trailing 5-4 but rallied against a trio of Astros relievers. Jose Lima (1-6) took the loss.

Marlins starter Alex Fernandez (15-8) allowed five runs -- three earned -- and nine hits in seven innings, walking three and striking out 10 in winning his fifth consecutive start. Robb Nen escaped a ninth-inning jam for his 30th save in 36 opportunities.
In St. Louis, Butch Huskey's run-scoring pinch single in the top of the 10th scored Edgardo Alfonzo with the go-ahead run as the New York Mets beat the Cardinals 5-4.

John Olerud had four hits for the Mets, who snapped a four-game losing streak and beat the Cardinals for the eighth time in 10 games. New York remained three games behind Florida in the N.L. wild card race.
John Franco survived a jam in the bottom of the 10th for his 30th save in 35 opportunities.
New Cardinals first baseman Mark McGwire homered twice and drove in three. He has three homers and six RBI in his last two games.

In San Diego, Mike Morgan overcame five weeks of poor pitching to allow one hit over seven scoreless innings and Stan Belinda and Jeff Shaw added an inning apiece to complete the shutout as the Cincinnati Reds edged the Padres 2-0.
Morgan (4-10), who retired the first 19 batters, walked one and struck out six. It was his first win since July 4 and followed a five-game losing streak in which his ERA was 5.74.
Joe Oliver had three hits for Cincinnati, which has won four of its last five games.
At Colorado, Mike Lieberthal's three-run homer highlighted a 4-for-5 performance as the red-hot Philadelphia Phillies pounded out a season-high 17 hits to beat the Rockies 12-8.
Mickey Morandini added four hits for Philadelphia, which has won four straight for the second time this season and is 12-3 in its last 15 contests.
